background.summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: comfortable with asymptotic analysis, basic algorithm design (divide and conquer, recurrences, the idea of FFT-style multiplication at the level of knowing it exists), discrete math (modular arithmetic, primes, gcd, binary representation), and linear algebra (vectors, matrices, subspaces, rank, dimension, invertibility). They know complex numbers and polynomials, and basic multitape Turing machines. They have not studied the specialist material of the paper: Harvey-van der Hoeven machinery, Gaussian resampling, Bluestein, Chinese-remainder multidimensional reindexing, Bruhat factorization, or precise fixed-point error analysis.
